utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As I indicated before, I would like to be sure, at least at the beginning of each week, whether there are still any problems remaining as far as providing the Defence with whatever exhibits that might be used during the next week. And I see everyone is still quiet, so I assume that it needs no special attention at this moment. I think then we could continue to examine Witness I. Would you please, Mr. Usher, bring in -- yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It's Mrs. Salcin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, yes, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From your answer, I do understand that you can hear me. Ms. Salcin, you were examined only for a rather brief period of time last Friday. I hope you had a good weekend. And we will now, as I indicated Friday --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- we will now continue. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Salcin, when we broke on Friday, you had described for the Trial Chamber the incident on 13 June in which you were shot. Could you please describe for the Trial Chamber where the bullet struck you.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bullet struck me in my right hand. My right hand, that was where the bullet hit me, through the palm. It entered through the palm and exited the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please describe for the Trial Chamber what you and Dzemal did after you were struck by the bullet, please.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: After you were struck by the bullet, can you please describe for the Trial Chamber what Dzemal and you did.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't feel that I had been hit straight away, not until there was a burst of gunfire, and then we all threw ourselves down on to the ground in the garden. We laid down. And when the shooting stopped, we got up. And it was only then that I realised that I had actually been wounded. And I looked at my skirt. It was all covered in blood. And then I saw my hand. It seemed to be all black. I couldn't remember anything much. But I just said to Dzemal, "I'm wounded," and Dzemal took me by the -- took hold of my hand like this and we went off.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went to a supermarket to look for a car to take me to hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were you successful in finding a car to take you to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A man said, "I'll take you," and that's what he did. He took us to Dobrinja to the hospital there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were you admitted into the hospital on that day?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was admitted by Dr. Mahmic, and straight away, he started to treat my wound.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately how long you remained in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the whole period?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed in hospital -- well, it was a long time ago, but about 15 or 16 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When you were discharged from the hospital, did the staff at the hospital give you any documents?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They gave me my diagnosis on the discharge sheet or whatever it's called.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would ask that the witness be shown the document marked P3369.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Salcin, I'd like you to look at the document that's been placed before you and tell the Trial Chamber whether or not you have seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Trial Chamber what this document is?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the diagnosis of my wounded hand. It contains my name and surname, my father's name, my date of birth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Salcin, does this document indicate the date that you were admitted into the hospital?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the 13th of June, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Salcin, I'd like to draw your attention now back to the day on which you were shot. Do you recall what you were wearing on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was wearing a leather jacket. I had a leather jacket on, and I had a blue skirt and black shoes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall what Dzemal was wearing on that day?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know if he was wearing a military uniform on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he wasn't. I know that for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were you carrying any type of military weapon on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Was Dzemal wearing any kind of military -- or carrying any kind of military weapon on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see any. No, quite sure he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall whether, in the immediate vicinity in which you were when you were shot, there were any soldiers or other people in uniforms?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there weren't. As far as I was able to see, no, there weren't any.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall if in the immediate vicinity at the time and place where you were shot, there was any type of military equipment or large weapons of any kind?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't notice any, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would ask at this time that the witness be shown the video which is Exhibit 3280F.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "INVESTIGATOR: Please stand where you were standing to the best of your recollection when you were shot. I will now use yellow paint to put an "X" on the spot where Mrs. Salcin has indicated. Mrs. Salcin, will you please assume the position you were in, to the best of your recollection, at the time you were shot. Please point in the general direction" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We seem to be having some technical problems with that videotape, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have any idea on how much time it would take -- we will wait for a few moments. Mrs. Salcin, we just have to wait for a second until the video is ready again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As far as I understand, the tape is damaged, which cannot be repaired right away. I think you have two options. First option is to continue even with a tape which is not perfect but the sound at least allows us to hear it. This is part of a longer videotape, as far as I understand, and we could play perhaps the original one. Or we continue and see whether the tape could be repaired.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, it's my understanding that Madam Registrar has an additional copy of this videotape. Perhaps we could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we perhaps could use that, then. Madam Registrar, has it been marked personally by you, since now the --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we in one way or the other identify it so that the tape that comes back is exactly the same as the tape that left the courtroom. Thank you very much. We'll just wait and see whether the authentic original has got the same damage which it should have as the copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "THE INVESTIGATOR: Please stand where you were standing, to the best of your recollection, when you were shot. I will now use yellow paint to place an "X" upon the spot that Mrs. Salcin has indicated. Mrs. Salcin, will you please assume the position you were in, to the best of your recollection, at the time you were shot. Please point in the general direction from which you heard gunfire at the time you were shot, to the best of your recollection. Please point in the general direction that you ran after you were shot."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Salcin, did you recognise yourself in that videotape?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you comply with the instructions of the investigator completely and truthfully, to the best of your ability?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my ability, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would ask that the witness be shown P3259, which consists of two photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you give the photos to the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask that the second of those photos, that is the one with the number 0211-4245, be placed on the ELMO first, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Usher, would you put the second photo. Yes, that's the correct one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Salcin, please take a look at that photograph. Do you see yourself in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Who is the other individual in the photograph next to you?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dzemal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Does that photograph accurately depict the location where you were standing when you were shot?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as it was a long time ago, I can't really remember. But I think it is. I think it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Does this photograph depict the street on which you were walking when you were shot?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: From there, yes, and I can see from Dobrinja as we were walking towards the Olympic place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Salcin, do you recall the name of that street upon which you and your brother-in-law were walking on that day?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it was Olimpijska. Now, whether they changed the name or not, I don't really know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, if you could please place the other photograph on the ELMO, that would be the one marked 0211-4239.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Salcin, can you see the photograph that has been placed in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Does this appear to be a close-up photograph of the prior photograph that you were looking at?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you see the houses located in the background of that photograph?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know what that area of Sarajevo is called?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: In the videotape, Mrs. Salcin, you indicated that the gunshot came from behind you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Looking at the photograph that's now in front of you, would the cluster of houses and buildings in the background represent the general direction from which the gunshot came?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I am able to remember, and as far as I know, it came from --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the interpreter did not catch the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please answer again? The interpreter could not hear you. Perhaps you can come a bit closer to the microphone. Mr. Usher, could you please assist? I think that's better. Could you please -- perhaps you could please put the last question again, Mr. Mundis, so that the witness can answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Salcin, looking at the photograph that's now in front of you, would the cluster of houses and buildings in the background represent the general direction from which the gunshot came?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Salcin, are you able to read maps?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I really can't. I couldn't do that in Sarajevo either. I don't find my way around a map easily.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would ask that the witness now be shown the 360 degree panoramic photo which is 3279E.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The computer evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Salcin, I'd like you to look at the screen in front of you. Do you recognise what's on the computer screen as being the street that you were on at the time you were shot?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see the pillar that was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If the photograph could please be panned slowly to the left, please? Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Does that refresh your memory, Mrs. Salcin?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. How can I describe this to you? From -- taking it from this pillar, we went downhill to the pink building down there, and that's where we fell. We fell here, when we heard the shooting, the shot. And when it was over, we went on again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When you mean "on again," towards which building or direction did you go?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Towards the buildings, the buildings on the right-hand side. That was where there was a supermarket and that's -- that was where we got the car that took us to the hospital. So we went across the parking lot. That's all I can remember. It was a long time ago, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could the photograph be panned to the left, please? Please stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Salcin, is this the direction from which you came on the day that you were shot? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was just shown, not this. I can't quite remember which part is Dobrinja and which part is Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: At the time that you were shot, Mrs. Salcin, were you walking up the hill that's depicted on the photograph in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This hill facing me, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So at the location where the camera is located, you were walking towards the camera; would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: One moment, please, Mr. President. I'm going to ask the technician to continue panning the photograph to the left, please. That's fine. Thank you. Mr. President, we have no further questions for the witness at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mundis. Ms. Pilipovic, I see you're nodding, so I expect the Defence to be prepared for cross-examination. Mrs. Salcin, now the Defence counsel will put some questions to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence wishes good morning to the witness.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Salcin, could you tell us how long have you been living in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 30 years.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us in which part of Sarajevo you lived?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean from when I arrived in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So if I understand, you've been living in that part of town for 30 years?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, about that time. I'm not quite sure. About. About 30 years. I was a tenant, renting.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us if you know the area where you live very well?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what that area of city is called and which street you live in?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Alipasino Polje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps it's a translation error but in lines 16 through 20 of the English transcript there is a bit of confusion based on the question, "How long have you been living in Sarajevo," and which part of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand your need for clarification, such that -- of course, I couldn't follow the original language but you asked -- the witness asked whether the question was about the place where she lived when she took up residence in Sarajevo, and then it continues,

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: "So if I do understand, I think you've been living in that area for 30 years." There is some confusion among those who follow the English language. Could you please verify that again, whether there was any change in residence during this period of approximately 30 years?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Salcin, in this area of town that you said was called Alipasino Polje, is that where you've been living for 30 years or did you live elsewhere before?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I lived in other areas, in Buljakov Potok, in Sokolje.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us how long have you been living in Alipasino Polje?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only if I could. I really cannot recall. I don't want to make a mistake. Possibly about 20 years.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know any more. It was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On that day when you were wounded, as you told us yourself, could you tell us on -- at what time of the day was it that you set off to make a visit?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the visit? I really cannot tell you. I don't know when that was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you go to make that visit on that day?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean when I was wounded?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's when it was. It was on the 13th of June, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us which route you took to make that visit? From your house, which streets did you take?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my house, I cannot remember. I can only remember on the way back. I really don't know where I went to get to Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you go to make that visit to Dobrinja by yourself?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I went by myself. And on the way back, I was going with Dzemal.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us in Dobrinja in which area -- in which part of Dobrinja were you for that visit, in which street?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the street. It's just right at the very beginning. I don't know the street really.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On that day when you went to Dobrinja for that visit, what kind of day was it? What weather was it like?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to Dobrinja, and I believe that it was about 9.00 in the morning. And I think it was about 6.00, perhaps - I'm not quite sure - as we went back. I'm not sure about the time. Perhaps Dzemal can remember better than I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether on that day there were any armed operations at the time when you were going to that visit?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I did not hear anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And when you were returning from your visit, before you heard the shot, did you hear any other shooting?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not hear any shooting, but only the moment when I was already wounded.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Salcin, do you remember about the time from a few years ago -- from 1995 to 2001, do you remember giving statements to the investigators of the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to give statements, but I really cannot remember. It was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If I tell you that you gave a statement on the 8th of November, 1995, to the investigators of the Tribunal, could you confirm that for me?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If I tell you that you gave a statement to the investigators of the Tribunal on the 5th of September, 2001 -- that is, 2000, that was last year - the year before - do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went there when they called me, but I couldn't really do it. I couldn't remember, and I couldn't really bring myself to think about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If I tell you that you gave a statement to the investigators of the Tribunal on the 12th of September, 2001, that is, last year in September, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that perhaps may sound silly, but I don't remember the order of them and when exactly I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you'll allow us, the Defence would like to show the witness the statement to the witness on the 12th of September, 2001, signed by Mrs. Salcin. And the Defence would like the witness to identify her signature on this statement, considering the Defence intends to ask the witness something about a portion of her statement. The statement is dated 12th of September, 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The number of the document, in English it's 0211-4239. And the second page is 0211-4240.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's just about to verify whether the witness recognises it. I don't think it has to be put on the ELMO, just whether it's her signature or not. Ms. Salcin, do you recognise your signature on these?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you please -- Ms. Pilipovic, I expect you to read some lines of it, and...

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And may I invite the parties to find a procedure where until now it's rather a formality on whether -- since I do understand that both the Prosecution and the Defence take the position, especially when the witness is confronted with earlier statements, that this is the statement, these are the signatures. Perhaps we could try to find a line of questioning which saves much time. I think the question, "Do you remember one or two statements and whether you have signed it" would be, I think, good enough a basis for cross-examining --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- additional problem whether there's any dispute about dates or whether the signature is really the signature of the witness. Perhaps you could speed it up for future witnesses. Now, we know, Ms. Salcin, that was not about you specifically. I was just talking to the parties on a very technical issue. You just have seen that you signed the statement, and Ms. Pilipovic will put some further questions to you in relation to that statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Salcin, at the question asked by my learned colleague at 9.36, that after you felt that you were wounded, that you had -- that you had -- went to lie on a part of a vegetable patch.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat that?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You said, "I did not feel that I was wounded until there was a machine-gun burst and we went to lay down in a vegetable patch."

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. First what I felt was that my hand sort of went up in the air, and I thought it was a -- that I had had a nerve cramping or something. And then there was a shot, and that's when we had to lie down until the shooting stopped, because I presume it was that machine-gun burst. And so we lay down, and then the shooting stopped. And then we rushed to the building, as I said, where this supermarket was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mrs. Salcin, I will ask you about a portion of a statement that you gave on the 12th of September, 2001. And this is paragraph 4 from the statement. And it starts with "last year." I will read line 3: "We heard a shot after which -- and then more shots, possibly a burst. From our location in the road, we ran into a trench."

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Salcin, could you reply whether you went to take shelter into a vegetable patch or a trench?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, it was a garden.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, on the 12th of September, 2001, whether you said you went to run into a trench? Does that mean that on that occasion you were not telling the truth?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I really cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. The possibilities outlined by my learned colleague exclude the possibility that it was a trench in a vegetable garden. We would ask that that be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could you please verify this, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you tell us whether in that vegetable garden -- were there any trenches in that garden?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really did not see that, but where I lay down, it was -- it was a garden, where there -- there were potatoes where we lay down, and as for the trenches, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us why, on the 12th of September, 2001, you said that you had run to a trench which was empty? You said you had run to an empty trench. Did you -- did you then -- what you actually said in the statement, does that mean it's not true, what you said?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as what I can remember, I really don't know. I cannot remember any more.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like to have the photograph shown to the witness, and the number is 02114244.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you please? That's the photograph of the two larger heads.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Salcin, can you see that photograph where you and your relative are standing? Could you tell us if this intersection and this part that can be seen behind you, is that what it looked like on that 13th of June in 1994, as far as you can remember?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember everything.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether, on this part of the road, there were any roadblocks on these streets, a protection?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not see -- I did not see them.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How often did you walk down this road?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went -- I walked there on that day, and I didn't go after that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether this part of neighbourhood that you told us was Nedzarici, whether, in 1994, whether it looked the way it looks on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like to ask her about a portion of the statement that she gave on the 12th of September, 2001, on the same page, and this is paragraph 6, and it is line 7. "As I am positioned in the photographs, the houses shown behind us are not in the same condition they were in on the day I was shot. Many of the houses and buildings have been rebuilt. There are many new roofs in the photos, which were not there on the day I was shot."

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you say this in the statement?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. The sentence that my learned colleague read out didn't end where she stopped reading, and we would ask that the full sentence be put to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please do so, Ms. Pilipovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. "I cannot say exactly which houses, however, have been changed. The main street shown behind in the photographs, running left-right, had some container barricades, but I cannot remember where they started and ended, how many there were, and what areas were protected by the barricades."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps I wasn't clear before with my objection. What Ms. Pilipovic has just done is read the remainder of that paragraph. However, the sentence which she first put to the witness has a phrase which my learned colleague, unintentionally I'm sure, but omitted to read to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please assist her in finding the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The sentence which in English begins, "Many of the houses and buildings have been rebuilt."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Many of the houses and buildings have been rebuilt. There are many new roofs in the photos, which were not there on the day I was shot."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that the part you're aiming at?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps it's an error in the translation of the witness statement but in the English version there is another phrase which continues from that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you then, please, perhaps with the assistance of the interpreters, see whether this is a translation problem or not, at that very moment. Ms. Pilipovic, would you -- I see Mr. Piletta-Zanin will be of great assistance, since he can at least read both of the languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I ask Mr. Mundis which Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. was the sentence which appears in the English text so that we can have a look?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: In the English, the full sentence reads, "Many of the houses and buildings have rebuilt. There are many new roofs in the photos, which were not there on the day I was shot, and many of the houses and buildings have an extra storey, which was not there."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I do understand it, it's about the extra storey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. The two texts do not appear absolutely one and the same, so perhaps I could ask the interpreters to check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, it depends. If Ms. Pilipovic intends to question about storeys, it's highly relevant. If, on the other hand, she intentions to question about roofs, then it might, at least at this moment, not be that relevant. At least it has now been -- it seems it has been established --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Your Honour, the Defence will submit the copy in English as well to the interpreters, if this is needed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I don't think so, so the fact that the Defence has established that there is a small portion which does not appear in the B/C/S version and does appear in the English version, if I'm correct, because I do understand that the Prosecution reads the English version. So there is a -- some extra in the English version which is not in the B/C/S version. Well, now, the question is whether this is relevant -- of course, it's always relevant that translations are correct -- but it's relevant for the questioning, for the cross-examination of the witness at this moment, if you'd say, Ms. Pilipovic, "I would like to pay attention to that aspect as well," or, "I would like to, if I would have known" --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have to ask the witness whether she speaks English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, then the Defence will only be using the B/C/S translation because it is the language which the witness understands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do agree with you that that's the version she signed and if there would be any reason for you later on to pay proper attention to the -- to pay attention to the extra, which is in the English version, of course, you will have the opportunity to do so, only being adverted to it -- now, Mr. Mundis?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness actually signs the English language version of the statements, notwithstanding the fact that the witness doesn't read that language. That's the policies that are employed by the Office of the Prosecutor with respect to taking witness statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I thank you to have informed the Chamber about this, but then, of course, the question remains how it was read to her. I assume that it was in her original language and I do not know whether you can inform us on whether at that moment, the prepared, written translation is used to read the statements to the -- the statement to the witness or that an interpreter is translating at that very moment from the B/C/S version into the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The standard procedure, Mr. President, would be the latter of the two options that you just presented.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that would mean that I do not understand, then, how, from the B/C/S version, you get something extra in the English version. So it's quite incomprehensible to me, if you start -- if you start with the B/C/S version and then translate it into English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps I wasn't clear, Mr. President. The statements are actually taken by an English-speaking investigator. The statement is then, with the use of a field interpreter, read back to the witness in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The witness then signs the statement. The statement is then brought back here to the Hague where it is then submitted for translation into written B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So we will never know exactly what the translation will have been in B/C/S at this spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The official translator will not know the oral B/C/S as spoken to the witness. They have to rely upon the written English version which the witness has signed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it may have been possible that even this extra part has been read to the witness already on the spot, and then it has been forgotten to be translated later on when the statement arrived in the Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, because the oral interpretation is done by a different person than the person who does the written translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I would say again our keyword will remain "precision." Ms. Pilipovic, you are now aware of some extra in the English version of the statement. You may continue to cross-examine the witness; and if there's any need to consider whether you want to question the witness also on the extra part, of course you'll get your opportunity to do so. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Salcin, did you understand what I read out to you from your statement of the 12th September, 2001?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't -- I don't really remember. Believe me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, perhaps it's good to read it again and perhaps -- unless you feel any need for it, just to leave out the stories at that moment. But you also may include it if you think it's relevant. Please read it again to the witness. Ms. Salcin, this may be a bit confusing for you, but there seems to be a small difference in the language -- the original language that you may have used and the English translation. We have been speaking about that for a couple of minutes, but you may just forget about it. Ms. Pilipovic will again read to you part of your statement as you signed it in September 2001, and then she'll put questions to you on that. It's no reason to be nervous about it. We'll settle the problem. You just answer the questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Salcin, I will read to you just one word. "Houses behind me are not exactly in the same shape as on the day that I was shot." Did you say this? Can you tell us from what you remember about that time in what shape, in what state, were the houses that we see here behind you? Can you explain that to us.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were in ruins. But this was done -- the rebuilding had begun and roofs are there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us if you know anything about how these houses were destroyed, the houses that you tell us were in ruins?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, during the war, there was destruction, and I can't really remember the time. But once the war was over, people started rebuilding their houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you told us that it was destroyed during the war, what part of the war? What period of time during the war do you have in mind when you say that?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that day when I went to Dobrinja, I saw this -- that the houses were destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who used to live there?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And before, you said that the houses were destroyed during the war. But before the war, did you used to visit this -- that neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what it is called?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, well, we called it Nedzarici. Whether this is...

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: During the 20 years that you spent in that area, in Alipasino Polje, you never visited this particular area, Nedzarici, did you?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: During the war - and I will remind you, it is 1992, 1993, 1994 - are you aware that in this part of the city that you live in, that is, Alipasino Polje and Nedzarici, was there any fighting there during the war?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Alipasino Polje, well, there was gunfire, naturally. But believe me, I didn't really pay much attention because I was concerned chiefly about my children.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On this photograph, can you show us where the monastery is on this photograph? Do you know where it is? That is, it is a place that you tell us the shot that wounded you came from. If you don't know, just tell us you don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President. I'm unaware of this witness indicating that the shot came from the monastery. She has testified that the shot came from behind her. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the objection is sustained.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise. I will find the place in the transcript during the break, the place where the witness said that the shot came from a monastery. But I will now move on to something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are pleased to get this information from you, Ms. Pilipovic. It is the recollection -- but we'll be glad to be corrected if we are wrong. It is the recollection of all three Judges that the witness has not been speaking about a monastery before. But of course, we can make mistakes as well. So please assist us. If you can find it during the break, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Salcin, you told us that your relative came back from Dobrinja with you that day. Can you tell us how are you related to the gentleman that was with you that day?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know how to explain that. I'd rather not -- well, let him say that. I'm not really much good at these relationships.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If I tell you that he's your brother-in-law, would that mean that he's your husband's brother?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Husband's brother. Once again, I can't say. I called him out of deference my brother-in-law. But now what kind of relationship that is, I can't say. He can explain it better.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How long have you known Mr. Dzemal?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: A long time.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where he worked?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know if he was a member of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. As regards his work, I know nothing about that. I didn't pay any attention.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you mostly concentrated and were concerned about your family, your children. Did your children live with you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection on two grounds, Your Honour: at what point in time did her children live with her, and also just in general the relevance of this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will ask if in 1993, in June, did your children live with you. And then I will explain why this is relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, usually if there is any objection about the relevancy, you should explain before. But on the other hand, it's a short question. Even if it turned out to be not very relevant, I don't see any problem in the question being answered. So the question to you was whether in June 1993 your children were living with you, Mrs. Salcin.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard that the witness said yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did your children go to school?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the answer or speak up.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How old were your children at that time in 1993?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't know anything any more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mrs. Salcin, you don't have to be nervous. We'll sort it out. We'll help you to give the proper answers. But perhaps first, Ms. Pilipovic, you are referring to June 1993, whereas the --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think you intended to ask about 1994, since that's the date of the --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, Your Honour. Yes, yes, of course. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you allow me to see, just to ask Mrs. Salcin? Mrs. Salcin, Ms. Pilipovic was asking you about the time when this incident happened. Do you remember whether at that period of time your children were living with you?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness speak up, please. We cannot hear her at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please perhaps assist the witness -- could you please come a bit closer to the microphone because the interpreters have difficulties in hearing you. Could you please put the microphone as close to the -- it's not possible to... Okay. Could you try to speak a bit louder as well, so that's easier for all of us to understand you. So in June 1994, your children were living -- how many children do you have?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had three, and I still do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So after the incident, you went to hospital. Do you remember how old your children were at that time approximately? Did they come and see you in hospital?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you remember still the age approximately when they were at your bedside?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I -- I can say -- I can tell you the years they were born. That is all. My daughter was born in 1971.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have noted down about my daughter?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: My older son, my son, 1975.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. And my other son, 1978.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the youngest son?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So we will know approximately their ages at the time when it happened. In 1994, your daughter must have been approximately 23 years old; your eldest son, 19 years old; and your younger son, 16 years old. Is that what you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did they go to school until what age? First, your daughter. Was she still at school when she was 23, or did she do something else?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. She didn't go to a school. She had come out, completed the secondary education, and that was it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And your son, your elder son, when did he leave Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. school, at what age?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: He completed two years, and the third one he didn't, because the war had started in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you'd say once the war started, he interrupted his school; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Nobody went to school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And your younger son, was that the same?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, he did go to school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: During the whole war?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember exactly at what time. Yes. I think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He continued going to school when the war was still going on?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when he could go, when the conditions were right, he went, and so it was like that, but he completed his schooling during the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Completed. Do you remember whether this was in the beginning of the war, at the end of the war?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I really -- I can't even remember any more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you don't know, just tell us. I just wondered whether he left school already when you were in hospital or not, your youngest son. You don't remember?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't. I don't remember, really can't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, merely for the transcript, merely for the transcript, on page 28, we see in the transcript, in the English transcript, it says 43:13, that the answer that the witness gave was not recorded, and I believe that what is in the French transcript, that the witness answered "yes" to that question, and it was -- and that is the only thing. Otherwise, the witness can continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have not yet found the page 28. Could you please tell us what question it was that the witness answered "yes" to in the French?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was very precisely -- the question was whether the children went to school, as you have just now explained, and the first question [as interpreted] was very clearly "yes."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Salcin, if I understood you well in that 1994, your children went to school, or is it only your younger son that was still in school, and your daughter and your older son were not in school?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us during the war, that is 1992, 1993 and 1994, what did your older son and daughter do? Were they employed anywhere?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were not employed. They were -- my daughter was -- was in the army, distributing food to the troops.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And what about your son?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the son was in the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So I gather that your daughter and your older son were in the army in 1992, 1993, 1994; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what army?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the BH, naturally.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us if your daughter and son, and I mean 1992, 1993, 1994, while they were in the BH army, did they wear uniforms?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: My daughter didn't, and not even my son, because there was a shortage of uniforms. He was chiefly in his own clothes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did he have any weapons?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not bring any when he came home. I don't know if he had any, because he was quite young.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where did your son spend his nights during that time that he served in the army, in 1992, 1993, 1994? Where did he sleep?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We could not hear the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what unit he belonged to? When I say "unit," I mean military formation. Where they billeted or where did he have to report?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, the interpreters have indicated to us that they could not hear an answer given by the witness. The question was put to you, Mrs. Salcin, on where your son spent his night during the time when he served in the army, where did he sleep, and we could not hear your answer. Could you please repeat your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know either. I'm rather -- can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the question is whether he usually came home to sleep or that he did not sleep in your home. I think that's especially what Ms. Pilipovic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, at times he came home, and at times he didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Just one question before the break: How often did your son come home? When I say "often," I mean a week, how often a week, a month. Would he come on a weekly basis or a monthly basis?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On a weekly basis.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And how often would he come home a week?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't even remember any longer, believe me.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you. I believe this is now a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pilipovic, how long would you still use because our rule is that cross-examination should not take more time. Cross-examination, even if I would deduct, well, let's say, eight to ten minutes, then you have taken already more time than the examination-in-chief took. Last Friday, it was approximately a quarter of an hour, the examination-in-chief, where we started a few minutes after 9.30, stopped at 10.05, so you've taken now approximately one hour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will do my best to reduce my cross-examination to a couple of questions -- with your leave, of course. We lost a lot of time for technical reasons during my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We lost time in the examination-in-chief as well on technical problems. Could we just see would you be able to choose the most relevant questions and, well, let's see, do it in five minutes? Or would that be -- okay. Then we'll --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will adjourn until 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, are you ready to proceed? Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Two issues, very, very briefly. First, for the record, Mr. Ierace, with the leave of the Trial Chamber, has temporarily excused himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's accepted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And perhaps more importantly, during the recess, Mr. President, one of the interpreters approached me and indicated that it is extremely likely that the witness did, in fact, use the term "monastery"; however, there was some uncertainty in the translation booth both because of the general inaudibility of the witness, and they simply weren't quite sure whether that term was actually used. So I simply wanted to put in the record that it is possible that the Defence counsel did, in fact, hear the witness say that, but that word was not, in fact, reflected in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that would mean that you withdraw your objection, but perhaps suggest that the question be phrased a bit more open than it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Absolutely. Or perhaps that it simply be clarified by asking the witness. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Pilipovic, I'm only too glad now that I gave you the opportunity to clarify the issue. And of course, since the objection has been withdrawn, then of course the decision that I sustained the objection, of course, doesn't exist any more. So you may proceed on that issue. But as it was suggested, and I give the same suggestion to you, that perhaps you try to find out a bit more about the earlier mentioning of the monastery. And I can imagine that since you will be following the original language, that there might have been this misunderstanding. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you wanted to add or to make any other observation?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Before Ms. Pilipovic takes the floor, I would sincerely like to thank the Prosecution for this type of intervention, which I think is perfectly along the lines of what one should do. And I hope that the Defence counsel will follow that line and course as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You appreciate that the other party is behaving in Court as you intend to do yourself. That's a great development. Ms. Pilipovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I should like the witness to be shown photograph 0211-4244, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Salcin, could you tell us, looking at the photograph, from what direction the shot came?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, from behind my back.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, looking at the photograph again, as you have just said that it came from the monastery, where on the photograph was the monastery located? Could you tell us in what section of this photograph? Could you point the monastery out to us?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know how to do that. I can't see very well either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you please help the witness to -- well, if you just see whether she could with the pointer, perhaps on the ELMO. Ms. Salcin, would you please look at your right-hand side where -- would you please look at the usher. No, if you would please look at the side. Please, first look to me. Yes. Would you please look to the right-hand side on that machine, and Mr. Usher will help you. You see there is that picture also and now you can indicate with this pointer where the monastery would be.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, for the record, the witness is indicating a white square building of which only the top can be seen. It is situated near to the right post, at approximately a quarter from the right of the picture, the white building just showing up a bit between the red roofs, to the left a higher tree. I think that's enough indication of where she pointed at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, perhaps marking is better than me wasting a lot of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness could perhaps be asked to draw a circle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please give her a black marker?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Salcin, could you draw a circle around the spot, please?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think she made a very small circle in the middle of that building she indicated before. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Salcin, in June, 1994, do you happen to remember whether, behind your back on this photograph, you see a large intersection, and do you know what it is?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please believe me when I say I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember any barricades being there in that month of June, 1994?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know that there was some kind of trench.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: This trench, which line did it follow on the photograph? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember now. It was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you indicate the spot where that was on the photograph, please? Those trenches, as you said. Can you show us where it was, roughly, on the photograph? Could you mark it in with a pen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mrs. Salcin, would you again look to the right where the usher is standing next to the other photo on this machine? Yes, could you -- yes, please. If, with the black marker, you could indicate where the trenches were. But perhaps the ELMO zoom out a bit so we have a better view on -- yes, and then, Mr. Usher, could you please -- yes, thank you. If you do not know, just tell us, and if you could indicate by marking where these trenches were, please mark them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't find my way here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that means that the witness seems not to be able to mark these trenches. Ms. Pilipovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Salcin, do you know -- the spot that you said you were hit, do you know what street that was, what the name of the street was?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We called it Nedzarici, now what -- Bosna Srebrena.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have two more questions for you. The incident that took place on the 13th of June, 1994, did you report it to the competent authorities? And when I say "the competent authorities," I mean did you report it to the police, or anybody from the army? Did you tell anybody what had happened to you?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because when it happened, I went straight to hospital in Dobrinja so that I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether any family member reported that, of your family?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness Dzemal Maljanovic, who is on the photograph with you, could you tell us where he lives? I'm asking you about the time in 1994 when he was with you. Where did he live then, in 1994?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you don't know where he lived?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. I really don't know, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us one more thing? Was your husband a member of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. The Defence has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you Ms. Pilipovic. Any need for re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Just two or three questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Salcin, do you remember at the time when you were shot, whether it was light outside or had the sun set yet?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, it was sort of -- it was -- you could still see. It was still visible, still a bit of daylight. It might have been about 6.00, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you remember, as you were walking along the streets that day, whether you saw any anti-sniping barriers or barricades of any kind?

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't. I don't really know. I can't remember. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: In response to some questions by my learned colleague, you replied that you didn't know what Dzemal did for a living.

utterances.speaker: FATIMA SALCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I really don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You've answered so many questions, the Judges have no additional questions to put to you, Mrs. Salcin. This means that we are at the end of your examination as a witness. We are aware that it's a long journey for you to come to The Hague. We also noticed that -- well, you might have been a little bit nervous now and then, which we fully understand because that's -- it's an entirely new environment for you. We'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and your willingness to answer all the questions, since the Judges will need answers on all questions for the decisions we'll have to take. So thank you very much for coming and I wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you then please lead the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, the Registrar informs me that the medical report has already been tendered into evidence during the testimony of I think it was Dr. Nakas. Was there any reason to tender the documents twice into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I understand that the application to have this document admitted into evidence has been withdrawn. Then, Madam Registrar, the other documents presented by the Prosecution were a set of photos -- I'll just leave it to you to get the right order.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: A set of two photographs bearing the number P3259; 360-degree CD, P3279E; videotape, P3280F.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I hope I don't have to repeat the Defence's position with respect to the video material, and the objection is that it is not complete. So this applies to each of the incidents and the material presented. We always have an objection, and stand by our objection for the same reasons. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you'll understand that admitting the videos into evidence is based upon the same considerations as been given before. Then, Mr. Mundis, you may call -- Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Before we have the following witness brought in to the courtroom, I should like to take advantage of this opportunity to examine a point of procedure. And we saw today that the transcripts, the English transcript and the English statement, statement in English, of people who frequently only speak the Serbian language are not always exact. There is more information in the English version than exists in the Serbian version, so perhaps we could begin by asking each witness whether they speak or read English. That might be prudent in view of the fact that the statements are in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The problem is that if the statement indicates that the statement has been read into his -- into the original language of the accused, of course, the signature is about the original language and not about having read the English version. But I do agree with you that we need to be very precise that we detect whatever differences there are between these versions. It is highly regrettable that there are differences. Then, Mr. Mundis, call your next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Next witness, Mr. President, is Dzemal Maljanovic, who will be testifying as to the same incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Mr. Maljanovic, the rules of procedures and evidence require you to make a solemn declaration at the beginning of your testimony. The text of this declaration will now be given to you by the usher. Would you please make that declaration aloud.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Maljanovic. Please be seated. Mr. Maljanovic, you'll first be examined by Mr. Mundis from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Maljanovic, for the record, can you please state your full name and spell your last name, please.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MALJANOVIC
utterances.text: Dzemal Maljanovic, M-A-L-J-A-N-O-V-I-C.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Maljanovic, can you please state your date of birth and the town or city in which you were born.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MALJANOVIC
utterances.text: The 21st of January, 1942, and the place is Jelec, Foca municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Maljanovic, how long -- withdraw that question. Mr. Maljanovic, when the war started in Bosnia, in what city were you living?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MALJANOVIC
utterances.text: Ilidza, that is one of the municipalities of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when the war started, for how long had you been living in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MALJANOVIC
utterances.text: The war began in 1992, and I had lived there since 1965.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you briefly describe for the Trial Chamber how the conditions of life in Sarajevo changed once the war began.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MALJANOVIC
utterances.text: The conditions changed very suddenly. There were barricades at every step you took practically. There was snipers from every side. There was a -- there were shortages of electricity, gas, water. And humanitarian aid rarely reached Sarajevo so that there was a great deal of hunger and general shortage of water and electricity. And life in Sarajevo was very difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Maljanovic, when the war broke out, what was your occupation?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MALJANOVIC
utterances.text: For the first month, when I was evicted from my house, I went across a river. The river is called Zeljeznice, and the place is Otes. And then I went to our army. Later on it was to become the BiH army, the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what did you do for the army?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MALJANOVIC
utterances.text: We dug trenches. We stood guard at the front lines. And in that first period, there was hardly any shooting, whereas the Serbs on the other side, at Jelanica, were digging in. And when they started digging in, they had the artillery as well. And they launched an attack on that place -- a small place called Otes. And in four or five days -- during four or five days, there was shelling and they took control of the place after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Maljanovic, when you worked for the army, were you doing so as a civilian or as a soldier?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MALJANOVIC
utterances.text: We didn't have any uniforms. Everybody wore what clothes they had, their own clothes. Sometimes they would give us some boots. But we dug trenches and stood guard up at the line, front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
